# sideby

> Run every AI coding account side by side. sideby is a Node CLI (npm package `sideby`, Node 22.18+) that starts Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build and pi with one isolated config directory per account, keeps skills, hooks and rules shared with the Main Account, repairs drift with `doctor`, and shows each account's quota and 7-day token usage from local records only (built in; no ccusage).

Key facts:

- One account = one directory. claude: `~/.claude` (main), `~/.claude-<name>`, selected by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. codex: `~/.codex`, `~/.codex-<name>`, `CODEX_HOME`. grok: `~/.grok`, `~/.grok-<name>`, `GROK_HOME`. pi: `~/.pi/agent`, `~/.pi-<name>/agent`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. The Main Account is named `main` and runs without the variable.
- Account ref: `<family>:<name>`; a bare `<name>` works when unique. Names match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`.
- Discovery: a directory matching the pattern is an account only if it holds `proxy.env` or at least one of the family's Shared Items (so `~/.claude-code-router` is not an account). Config `ignore` skips refs.
- API account: an account directory containing `proxy.env` (dotenv subset, mode exactly 600). Its variables reach only the launched Host. Login state is `not-needed` (`key` in `sideby list`). Exception: pi loads `proxy.env` for provider keys, but a pi account stays a subscription account and signs in with `/login`.
- sideby never switches a global active account, never reads credentials to call a model, never proxies or pools logins, and never calls private quota endpoints. `sideby next` only recommends the next account from local quota data; a person starts it. Only Auto Handoff (config `handoff.auto`, off by default; ADR-0010) moves a running task to another account by itself.
- Agents must not read `proxy.env`, `auth.json` or `.claude.json`, and must let the user run `sideby login <ref>` themselves. sideby itself reads only identity fields there (email, Claude organization; the `email` claim of Codex's `id_token`), never a token value (ADR-0003); `sideby list` shows them.
- What a new account shares (`sideby families <family> --json` gives the same for the user's machine, plugin families and config `extraSharedItems` included). claude: links `settings.json`, `settings.local.json`, `skills`, `commands`, `plugins`, `hooks`, `themes`, `CLAUDE.md`; keeps only the `mcpServers` entry of its own `.claude.json` equal to `~/.claude.json`. codex: links `AGENTS.md`, `hooks.json`, `plugins`, `rules`, `skills`; `config.toml` linked (or a synced copy) for subscription accounts, the account's own for API accounts. grok: links `skills`, `installed-plugins`; copies `hooks`, `hooks-paths` and a subscription account's `config.toml` (Grok refuses links there); `trusted_folders.toml` is copied once, then the account's own. pi: links `AGENTS.md`. Never shared: sign-in (`auth.json`, Keychain, the rest of `.claude.json`), sessions and history. Items the Main Account lacks are skipped.

## Set up sideby for a user

Users ask "install sideby", "set up another Claude account, cc008". Do every step yourself except those marked **user**; for those, give the user exactly one line to run (in Claude Code they can type `! <command>`).

1. `node --version` must be 22.18 or newer; otherwise tell the user to upgrade Node and stop. npm's `engines` warning (`EBADENGINE`) does not stop the program. sideby exits 1 itself below 22.18, including `--help` and `--version`; `statusline-tap` still runs the original status-line command. `sideby --version`; if it is missing, `npm i -g sideby` (a global install is needed for Claude quota and shell functions).
2. `npx skills add Adonis0123/sideby -g` installs the sideby skill so later requests go through it.
3. `sideby list --json`: `families[].installed` says which Host CLIs are on PATH. For a Host that is not installed, give the user its `installCommand` (an official one-line installer, when the Family has one) or its `installUrl`, and stop; never install a Host unasked. `brokenBin` means the Host is on PATH but cannot run (often a link left by an interrupted upgrade): reinstalling fixes it. If the Host has no Main Account yet, ask the user to start it once (for example `claude`); `new` needs the Main Account.
4. `sideby families <family> --json`: tell the user in a sentence or two what the new account will share and that its sign-in, sessions and history stay its own.
5. Create it. With a name from the user: `sideby new <family> <name> --json`. Without one: `sideby new <family> --next --json`, which picks the next number (`008` after `001`…`007`) and a short command following the existing ones (`cc008`; see `suggestion`). Add `--alias <short>` when the user named a short command, and `--api` for an API account.
6. **user**: subscription account: `sideby login <ref>` (browser sign-in; for pi it starts pi, then they type `/login`). API account: the user fills in the `proxy.env` path that `new` printed; never read or write it yourself.
7. Make short commands work in new terminals: when the config has no `shellInitFile` and the user's `~/.zshrc` (bash: `~/.bashrc`) has no `sideby shell-init` line, say so and append `eval "$(sideby shell-init zsh)"` (or `bash`) to it.
8. Verify: `sideby doctor <ref> --json` (`status: "ok"`), and after the user signed in, `sideby list --json` shows `login: "logged-in"` for the account.
9. Optional, Claude only, when the user wants quota: `sideby quota setup claude` exits 10 with a diff; show it, and only after a yes run it again with `--yes`.

Finish by telling the user how to start it: the short command in a new terminal, or `sideby run <ref>`.

## Commands

- `sideby` / `sideby list [--json]`: list accounts (TYPE `main`|`sub`|`api`, LOGIN `✓`|`login needed`|`key`|`?`, EMAIL, MODEL, DIR, and on macOS DESKTOP `open` when that account's desktop app window runs). `--json` accounts carry optional `identity: { email?, org? }` and `sameLogin: [ref]`: the other accounts signed in as the same login (Claude only: same email and organization), which share one quota (spec §3.21); the table marks them as `claude:001 = main`. Problems plugins hit while reading an account go to stderr. Exit 0.
- `sideby run <acct> [-- args]`: start the Host for one account. Exit: Host's code; 128+n if killed by signal n; 1 on sideby error. Argument order: family defaults, the family's `keepTitle` args (only with config `accountTitle`), `accounts.<ref>.args` from config, the alias's `args` when `<acct>` is an alias, then user args. The Host gets `SIDEBY_ACCOUNT=<ref>` and `SIDEBY_LABEL` (the alias it was started through; else the account's alias, those without args first; else the ref) for a status line or prompt; both are set on every launch (`run`, `next`, `login`, a routed `resume`). With config `accountTitle: true` the terminal title becomes `[<SIDEBY_LABEL>]` and Codex gets `-c tui.terminal_title=[]` so it keeps it.
- `sideby new <family> <name>|--next [--api] [--alias <short>] [--json]`: create an account. `--next` picks the name instead: the next number after the highest numbered account with the same width (`001`…`007` → `008`), else `work`, `work2`, …; without `--alias` it also adds a short command when the family's existing aliases show a prefix-plus-name pattern (`cc007` for `claude:007` → `cc008`), and leaves it out, with the reason in `suggestion.aliasProblem`, when that name is taken or reserved. A name together with `--next` exits 2. `--alias` also adds `<short> → <family>:<name>` to config `aliases` (sideby writes only `aliases` and `handoff` in the config: `aliases` here and in `sideby alias`, `handoff` in `sideby handoff enable|disable`; keys and order kept, refused when the config is not valid JSON); an invalid, reserved or taken alias is refused before anything is created. After creating, every configured `shellInitFile` is rewritten. Exit 0; 1 partly failed, invalid name, or the alias was not added (the account still exists).
- `sideby alias add <short> <acct> [-- host args] [--json]`: add a short command for an existing account. `<acct>` may be a ref, a unique name or an alias; the config stores the ref, as a string, or as `{ account, args }` when host args follow `--`. Only `sideby run <short>` adds those args; other commands just resolve the account. Rewrites every `shellInitFile`. Exit 0 (`status` `added`, or `exists` when identical); 1 when the name is invalid or reserved, the account does not exist, or the name already starts something else (remove it first). `sideby alias rm <short> [--json]`: exit 0 (`removed` or `absent`). Aliases never carry environment variables.
- `sideby login <acct>`: run the family's sign-in command with the account selected; for pi, start pi and print "type /login". Exit: Host's code.
- `sideby next <family> [--dry-run] [--include-api] [--json] [-- host args]`: Handoff. Rank the family's accounts by Quota Pressure (used percent of the fullest window not reset yet) and start the lowest, as `sideby run` would. States: `ready` (subscription, under 85%), `unknown` (no quota data; ranked after ready), `api` (only with `--include-api`), `full` (a live window at 85%+), `logged-out`. `--dry-run` and `--json` only recommend. When no account has quota data (`hasQuota: false`) nothing starts and the exit code is 1. Claude and Codex; families without a quota source fail with code `no-quota-source` and list their accounts. Exit: Host's code when started; 0 for `--dry-run`/`--json` with a pick; 1 when nothing can be picked, no account has quota data, no quota source or no accounts. The new account starts a new session; sessions are not copied. Accounts of the same login share one quota; run inside a session sideby started (`SIDEBY_ACCOUNT`), `next` never picks an account of that session's same login.
- `sideby doctor [acct|family] [--fix] [--force] [--json]`: check Shared Items, credential modes, leftovers, and whether the sideby skill each checked family's Host reads (`<main>/skills/sideby`, plus `~/.agents/skills/sideby` for Codex) matches this version (`skill.outdated`, general warn on that family's main account). Exit 0 when no `fail` Finding (warnings allowed); 1 otherwise.
- `sideby quota [acct|family] [--refresh] [--json]`: quota windows and 7-day usage, in the Display Order. Grok quota (spec §3.26, ADR-0025) is asked from the `grok` CLI of each signed-in subscription account (`grok agent --no-leader stdio`, method `_x.ai/billing`; the Host sends the request with its own login, sideby reads no credential), at most every 15 minutes per account and kept in `<state>/quota/<family>/<name>.fetched.json`; the newer of that and the Grok log's billing line is shown; `--refresh` asks again now; off with config `quota.check.<family>: false` or in CI (`reason: not-enabled`). A failed ask is `reason: fetch-failed` with `detail`, or `fetchError` on the last good reading (`fetched: true`). A window may carry `name` (models it covers, such as a plugin's "Other models"); named windows do not count toward Quota Pressure. Accounts of the same login show the freshest reading of the login, with `from: <ref>` when it was read from another account; usage stays per account. Exit 0.
- `sideby quota setup claude [--yes] [--json]`: without `--yes`, print the diff and change nothing; with `--yes`, wrap `statusLine.command` in `~/.claude/settings.json` as `sideby statusline-tap --orig-b64 <base64>` (or `sideby statusline-tap` when there was none). Refused (exit 1) if `sideby` is not on PATH or comes from the npx cache: needs `npm i -g sideby`. Exit 10 when it only showed the change (rerun with `--yes` after the user agrees); 0 applied or already enabled; 1 blocked or failed.
- `sideby tune [acct|family] [--json]`: estimate the cheapest auto-compact threshold per model from the last 7 days of local session records. Claude gets a suggested `autoCompactWindow`; Codex only observations; Grok and pi no source. An estimate; nothing changes until `sideby tune apply <acct> [tokens] [--yes] [--json]` (without `--yes` it prints the file, the change and which accounts share the file, and exits 10; show it to the user and only then rerun with `--yes`; writes one key, `autoCompactWindow`, of the account's `settings.json`) and `sideby tune undo <acct> [--yes]`. Exit 0; 1 unknown account or family, blocked, nothing to undo; 2 extra arguments.
- `sideby model <acct> [<model>|default] [--effort <level>|default] [--yes] [--json]` (spec §3.19): the model and effort the account runs with, each `{ value, from }` with `from`, first match wins, `sideby` (the account's arguments in the config), `last` (the newest session) or `host` (Claude `settings.json` `model` / `modelSettings.<model>.effortLevel` / `effortLevel`; Codex `config.toml` `model` / `model_reasoning_effort`); a change edits only the model and effort arguments in config `accounts.<ref>.args` (exit 10 without `--yes`); never writes a Host file; not for API accounts.
- `sideby remote-control [on|off|undo] [--yes] [--json]` (spec §3.22, ADR-0017): each Claude settings file (accounts linking to one file share it) with `state` on (`remoteControlAtStartup` true: sessions connect to claude.ai/code and the Claude app by themselves), default (not set), off, missing (no settings.json: run `sideby doctor --fix`), blocked. `off` writes `remoteControlAtStartup: false` into every on or default file, one key only; `on` writes `true` into every off or default file (only when the user asks: every device signed in to the account can then read new sessions); `undo` restores the old value while the key still holds what sideby wrote. Without `--yes` each prints the change and exits 10; show it to the user first. `/remote-control` in a session still works; running sessions stay connected until restarted. Exit 0; 1 blocked, failed or nothing to undo; 2 bad arguments.
- `sideby quota teardown claude [--json]`: restore the original bytes, only if the file is unchanged since setup; otherwise refuse with a diff. Exit 0; 1 refused or failed.
- `sideby ui [--port n] [--no-open]`: local panel on `127.0.0.1:17420`; reuses a running sideby panel, shifts past busy ports.
- `sideby ui --background [--port n] [--no-open]`: start the panel detached from the terminal (pid and log in the state directory; Hosts found through the login shell's PATH), or reuse a running one (replaced when it runs another build, so an upgrade takes effect), then open it. An open panel page reloads itself when the server runs another build (`build` in `/api/state`). `sideby ui --stop`: stop it, only after checking the pid is a sideby panel. Exit 0; 1 if it could not start or stop.
- `sideby desktop <acct> [--json]` (spec §3.20, macOS only): open the Family's Desktop App as that account: Claude Desktop (bundle id `com.anthropic.claudefordesktop`) for claude, the Codex app (`ChatGPT.app`, `com.openai.codex`) for codex. The Main Account opens with `open -n -a <app>` (the default data folder); any other subscription account with `open -n`, its select variable (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME`, plus `CODEX_ELECTRON_USER_DATA_PATH`) and `--user-data-dir` at `~/Library/Application Support/sideby/<family>/<name>/` (mode 700). An account whose window already runs is brought to the front (`action: "focused"`, or `already-running`), never started twice; sideby never ends a process, never modifies the app bundle, writes nothing into Host account dirs. A new Claude app data folder gets `claude_desktop_config.json` linked to the Main Account's default one (Doctor checks it as `app-data/claude_desktop_config.json` under `link` rules, except that a real file there, which the app writes itself, is checked only for its `mcpServers` key under `json-key` rules, as `app-data/claude_desktop_config.json#mcpServers`). Agent-session variables (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, `CODEX_COMPANION_*`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX*`) are cleared before `open`. A new account's sign-in screen may suggest the main account ("Welcome back" in the Codex app); tell the user to choose another account. Output `{ ref, family, app, appPath, action, appData?, createdAppData, linked[], command?, notices[] }`; relay `notices` (first sign-in: close other Claude Desktop windows). Exit 0; 1 with code `not-macos`, `no-desktop-app`, `api-account`, `app-not-installed`, `open-failed`; 2 missing argument.
- `sideby desktop grok-bot[:<name>] [--remove [--yes]] [--json]` (spec §3.20 "Grok Bot 窗口", ADR-0019, macOS only): Grok Bot (`Grok Bot.app`, `com.anysphere.sand`) signs in with a Cursor account, apart from every Account (not Grok Build), so its windows are App Profiles, not Accounts. `grok-bot:<name>` opens that window, creating `~/Library/Application Support/sideby/grok-bot/<name>/` (mode 700) first when the name is new; `grok-bot` / `grok-bot:main` is the app's default data. Opens with `open -n -a <app> --args --user-data-dir=<folder>`, `SAND_DATA_ROOT` / `SAND_USER_DATA_DIR` cleared; a running window is brought to the front. Same output as `desktop` (`family: "grok-bot"`); bad name `code: invalid-name`. `--remove` without `--yes` exits 10 with `{ ref, app, appData, removed: false }`, with `--yes` deletes the folder (`removed: true`); refuses `main-profile`, `app-running` (also when `ps` fails), `no-profile`, `app-data-invalid` (a link or file; never followed). `sideby list --json` has top-level `appProfiles: [{ ref, app, name, isMain, appData?, installed, running, signedIn? }]`; `signedIn` is the app's own `desktop-status.json` flag (last known), the signed-in email is never read. `sideby desktop grok:<acct>` is `no-desktop-app` and points at `grok-bot:<name>`.
- `sideby browser [--enable|--disable] [--yes] [--json]` and `sideby browser open <acct> [--profile <folder|name|email>] [--json]` (spec §3.24, ADR-0023, Google Chrome on macOS, and in WSL the Chrome installed on Windows): Browser Sign-ins, off until config `browser.signIns` is true (`--enable` shows what is read, exit 10; `--yes` writes it). While on, sideby reads only `Local State` (each profile's folder, display name and, when it is an email, `user_name`: the Google account it uses in Chrome) and the Local Storage key names (never values) of `https://claude.ai` and `https://chatgpt.com`; never cookies, Login Data, IndexedDB or the Keychain, no network. A profile signed in to an Account when a key name holds, as a whole segment, Claude's `oauthAccount.accountUuid` or Codex's `id_token` claim `chatgpt_user_id` (else `user_id`); the ids are compared in memory and never output. Output `{ enabled, browser, found, profiles: [{ dir, name, email?, signIns: [ref], changedAt? }], families: { matched, openOnly }, problems }`, newest change first; a match may be left from before a sign-out. Grok is `openOnly`. `open` runs `/usr/bin/open -na <Chrome.app> --args --profile-directory=<dir> <url>` (in WSL: `cmd.exe /d /c start "" <chrome.exe> --profile-directory=<dir> <url>`, folders from one `cmd.exe /d /c echo %LOCALAPPDATA%...` call) (claude.ai, chatgpt.com, grok.com) for the only matching profile or `--profile`; output `{ ref, url, profile: { dir, name }, command }`. Exit 0; 1 with code `unsupported`, `no-website`, `not-installed`, `no-profiles`, `profile-needed`, `profile-unknown`, `profile-ambiguous`, `open-failed`. The Panel shows the matched browser user's Google account (else its name) after each account's email; a click opens it.
- `sideby app install [--url <url>] [--json]`: panel launcher that runs `ui --background` (or opens `<url>`): macOS `~/Applications/sideby.app` (bundle id `dev.sideby.panel`), Linux `~/.local/share/applications/sideby.desktop`. Records the current Node and sideby paths; `sideby update` runs it again, so run it yourself only after upgrading Node or installing sideby another way. Without `--url` it keeps an address an earlier `--url` install recorded (uninstall, then install, to drop it). `sideby app uninstall [--json]` removes only files it created. Exit 0; 1 on an unsupported platform or a foreign file in the way.
- Library: `createPanelHandler({ runtime, basePath?, allowedHosts, readOnly?, theme?, lang?, updates? })` mounts the panel in another local Node server. `theme` is `{ colorScheme?: 'auto'|'light'|'dark', header?: 'plain'|'bar', light?: PanelThemeTokens, dark?: PanelThemeTokens }`; tokens (for example `font`, `bg`, `surface`, `primary`, `onPrimary`, `radius`, `controlHeight`, `gutter`; full list in `src/panel/theme.ts`) become CSS custom properties in the nonce'd style. Unknown tokens and values with characters outside letters, digits, spaces and `# % ( ) , . + - / ' " _` throw a TypeError. `lang` is `'auto'|'en'|'zh'` (default `auto`: the language picked in the panel, then the browser's); `en` or `zh` wins and hides the panel's language switch, and any other value throws a TypeError. It is read when the handler is created; create it again to switch. `updates` (default true) shows the update label, dialog and Auto Update switch; `false` hides them and refuses `/api/update*` with 403. `<basePath>/icon.svg` serves the sideby mark for a Portal's tab; `<basePath>/favicon.svg` the small cut.
- `sideby shell-init zsh|bash`: one shell function per account (`sideby-<family>-<name>`) plus config `aliases`, each calling `sideby run '<alias>'` so the config stays the source (commands that take an account, such as `run` and `doctor`, also accept an alias). Use `eval "$(sideby shell-init zsh)"`. `sideby shell-init [zsh|bash] --write` rewrites the configured `shellInitFile` with that output (exit 1 when none is configured or a file was not written; a file whose first line is not the shell-init header is never overwritten).
- `sideby resume <family> [-- host args]`: what the Host-named shell function calls. When the arguments resume a session by UUID (Claude and Grok `--resume <id>`, `--resume=<id>`, `-r <id>`; Codex `resume <id>`), start the non-main Account that holds it (Claude `projects/*/<id>.jsonl`, Codex `sessions/**/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl`, Grok `sessions/*/<id>/`; newest write wins) exactly as `run` would, with a note on stderr. When no Account holds a Claude session but one started it (`session-env/<id>/`; the session never got a message), drop the by-id resume and start a new session in that Account (`run` for a non-main one, the Host with only those arguments removed for the Main Account), with a note on stderr (ADR-0009). Otherwise, or when the Family's select variable is already set, run the Host unchanged. Exit: the Host's code; 1 for an unknown Family or one that cannot route (pi). With config `resumeRouting: true`, `shell-init` also prints `function <bin> { … }` for each routable Family that has a non-main Account, unless an Alias has that name; it calls `sideby resume` only when the select variable is unset and an argument is UUID-shaped (or `--resume=<uuid>`), otherwise the Host directly.
- `sideby plugins [--json]`: loaded plugins and load errors. Exit 0; 1 if any failed.
- `sideby update [--yes] [--json]` (spec §3.23, ADR-0021): ask the npm registry now for the `latest` sideby and show `current`, `latest`, `available`, `method` (`kind` npm, pnpm, bun, volta, npx, project, source or local, a Local Build from `pnpm local` in a checkout whose `command` is `pnpm local --off`; `canUpdate`, `reason`, `reasonCode`, `reasonAt`), `command`, `canRun`, `releaseNotes`. Up to date: exit 0. Without `--yes`: exit 10 (ask the user first). With `--yes`: run `command` (npm, pnpm or bun global installs only), restart a running background panel (`restartedPanel`), run `sideby app install` again from the new version when the desktop app is installed (`refreshedApp`), exit 0; `skillUpdate` (`installed`, `outdated`, `command`, `canRun`, `reason`, `reasonCode`) is the installed sideby skill, which the Update brings along with `npx -y skills update sideby -g -y` (`skillUpdated` in the result; with the CLI current, `sideby update` offers the skill alone); a skill in a git repository is left alone unless the skills tool's `.skill-lock.json` records installing it there (`canRun: false`, `reasonCode: skill-in-git`, give the user `command`). `canRun: false` exits 1: give the user `command` to run. Registry unreachable or install failed: exit 1. Update Check: once a day, after a command on a terminal (never with `--json`), sideby asks `<registry>/-/package/sideby/dist-tags` (`SIDEBY_UPDATE_REGISTRY` overrides the registry) in a detached process and prints one stderr line on a later run; every `--json` output then carries `_notice.update` (`current`, `latest`, `command: "sideby update"`), and `_notice.skill` (`command: "sideby update"`) when the installed sideby skill is for another version: finish the task, mention it once, and offer to update (run `sideby update --json`, then `--yes` after the user agrees); off with `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, `SIDEBY_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, config `update.check: false`, CI or a Local Build. Config `update.auto: true` (off by default; do not turn it on unless asked) installs a newer version of the same major after the check when no `sideby run`, `next` or `resume` is running, together with the skill, and brings a skill behind a current sideby up to date by itself; with it off, a terminal gets one line a day while the skill is behind.
- Auto Handoff (config `handoff`, spec §3.17): `auto` (default false; API accounts of any family and other families' accounts listed in `order`), `sameFamily` (default false; also the same family, the kind vendors may act on), `prepareAt` 80, `threshold` 95 (Quota Pressure in percent), `adaptive` true (each window hands over when it has less room than 1.5 times its largest turn of the run's last 5, between `prepareAt` and 99; before a turn is measured, or with false, at `threshold`; ADR-0032), `waitIfResetWithinMinutes` 30 (waits only when the session continues by itself at the reset: Claude with `autoContinueAtUsageLimit` not false in the account's `settings.json`; Codex and Grok never wait; the user sees a `systemMessage` at the threshold and a desktop notification at the limit, and `! sideby handoff ready` typed in the session moves on at once), `countdownSeconds` 10, `crossOrganization` (refs or aliases that may take over from another organization; organizations are compared by `org`, else email domain), `families.<family>`: `{ policy: "pressure"|"order", order: [ref|alias] }`. Only interactive sessions that sideby started, with stdin a TTY and a `sideby` on PATH that answers `sideby handoff-hook --check` with `ok` (sideby's arguments go before the user's first `--`); an account already at `threshold` counts as full; an account of the origin's same login is skipped, also when `order` names it, and the terminal says why; never headless runs, Codex `--remote`, Grok `strict` or custom sandbox profiles. sideby stays the Host's parent: it sets `SIDEBY_HANDOFF_RUN`, `SIDEBY_HANDOFF_FAMILY`, `SIDEBY_HANDOFF_DIR` and adds hooks (Claude `--settings <state>/handoff/claude-settings.json`, Codex `-c hooks.PostToolUse=…`/`-c hooks.Stop=…`, Grok a hook file from `handoff setup`). The hidden `sideby handoff-hook <family> <event>` (PostToolUse, Stop, StopFailure) asks the session to write its brief at `prepareAt`, to finish when a window reaches its level (the message names the window, its percent and reset time; the brief counts as finished only with the last line `<!-- handoff brief complete -->`), and writes `ready.json`; a StopFailure counts only for a used-up quota, never a transient rate limit. sideby then ends the Host (SIGTERM, 10 s grace, never SIGKILL), finishes the brief (adds branch, uncommitted files, diff stat; assembles one from the session's records when needed), counts down (Enter stays and resumes the old session), and starts the next account with `--add-dir <chain dir>` (Claude, Codex) and the brief's path as the first prompt after `--`. Files: `<state>/handoffs/<chain>/` (mode 700; `plan.json`, `run-<id>.json`, `ready.json`, `request.json`, `waiting.json`, `chain.json`, `<n>-<ref>.md` briefs, mode 600). Starts: Claude (quota and limit; needs `quota setup claude`), Codex (quota; trust the hooks once per account in `/hooks`), Grok (quota and limit; needs `handoff setup grok` and `doctor grok --fix`; sandbox `off`/`devbox` start, `workspace`/`read-only` only receive). pi only receives. Plugin families can only receive.
- `sideby handoff status [--json]`: read-only readiness: `auto`, `sameFamily`, `prepareAt`, `threshold`, `sideby: { ok, problem? }` (the `sideby` on PATH can run the hook), `families[]` (`family`, `starts`, `ready`, `problems[]`, `notes[]`, `order: { policy, order, unknown[] }`), `nextSteps[]` (commands in order). Exit 0. `sideby handoff enable [--same-family] [--no-same-family] [--order <family>=<acct,…>] [--prepare-at n] [--threshold n] [--wait-minutes n] [--countdown n] [--yes] [--json]` / `sideby handoff disable [--yes] [--json]`: change only the config `handoff` key (other settings kept): exit 10 with the change shown (`diff`), 0 once written or already so, 1 for an unknown `--order` account (`code: unknown-account`); `--json`: `{ applied, file, diff, settings, nextSteps }`. Agents run `status`, then `enable` and ask before `--yes`, then each `nextSteps` entry. With Auto Handoff off, `sideby run` prints a one-line pointer to `handoff status` at most once a day when the account ended past the threshold, and the Panel shows a hint and an Auto Handoff dialog (`/api/handoff/status`, `/api/handoff/configure` with `confirm`).
- `sideby handoff ready [--to <account>] [--brief <file>] [--json]`: inside a session sideby started with Auto Handoff, hand over to the next account when this turn ends; prints (JSON `next`) the account that takes over, which can differ from `sideby next` because the chain never goes back to an account it used; `--to` names the account, also one the chain already used (hand back), and fails with `no-pick` rather than picking another; `--brief` copies the user's own note into the chain directory; a manual request never waits for a reset, and while the session waits for its quota (`waiting.json`) it hands over at once (JSON `now: true`). Exit 0; 1 outside such a session (`code: not-in-handoff-run`) or when the brief cannot be read (`brief-unreadable`). `sideby handoff setup <family> [--yes] [--json]` / `teardown`: the hook file for a Host without a launch option (Grok): exit 10 when it only showed the change; teardown removes the file only while unchanged. Exit 1 also when no account can take over now (`no-pick`; nothing is written). Doctor warns (`handoff.no-quota-tap`, `handoff.setup-missing`, `handoff.order-empty`, `handoff.order-unknown`) only when `handoff.auto` is on.
- `sideby families [family] [--json]`: each loaded family (plugins included): `layout` (`main`, `account` relative to HOME), `selectVar`, `login` (`args` or null, `hint`), `quota`, `usage`, `quotaSetup`, and `shared[]` (`path`, `mode`, `key?`, `mainPath?`, `credential?`, `noSymlink?`, `source` `family`|`config`, `meaning`: one fixed sentence on what the item is in each account). Exit 0; 1 unknown family; 2 more than one family.
- `sideby <command> --help` (or `sideby help <command>`) prints help with examples for `new`, `alias`, `login`, `doctor` and `families`; other commands print the general help.
- Any command: exit 2 on a usage error (unknown option, missing argument); 1 when sideby fails (unknown account, invalid config); 10 when a change was shown and needs confirmation (`quota setup`, `handoff setup`, `update` or `browser --enable|--disable` without `--yes`).

## JSON contract

- `list`, `new`, `next`, `alias`, `doctor`, `quota` (with `setup`/`teardown`), `handoff`, `families`, `plugins` `app` and `desktop` accept `--json`; `run`, `resume`, `login`, `ui` and `shell-init` do not.
- Every JSON output has `schemaVersion: 1`. Adding fields keeps the version; removing, renaming or changing meaning bumps it. With `--json`, errors print `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "error": "...", "code": "..." }`: `code` is `usage` for a malformed command line, a reason such as `no-quota-source`, `no-accounts` or `alias-invalid`, or `error`.
- JSON Schemas for each output and for the config file ship in the package under `schemas/` (`list`, `new`, `next`, `alias`, `doctor`, `quota`, `quota-setup`, `quota-teardown`, `handoff-status`, `handoff-enable`, `handoff-disable`, `handoff-ready`, `handoff-setup`, `handoff-teardown`, `families`, `plugins`, `app-install`, `app-uninstall`, `desktop`, `error`, `config`).
- `list --json`: `families[]` (`id`, `title`, `bin`, `installUrl`, `installCommand?`, `installed`, `brokenBin?`, `plugin`), `accounts[]` (`family`, `name`, `ref`, `dir`, `isMain`, `kind` `subscription`|`api`, `secretFile?`, `familyTitle`, `hostInstalled`, `login` `logged-in`|`logged-out`|`unknown`|`not-needed`, `model?`, `problems?` string[], `desktopApp?` { `app`, `installed`, `running` } on macOS for subscription accounts of claude and codex), `pluginErrors[]` (`where`, `message`).
- `doctor --json`: `status` `ok`|`issues`, `accounts[]` (`ref`, `family`, `name`, `kind`, `dir`, `shared` {`ok`, `total`}, `backups`, `findings[]`), `general[]`, `fixes[]` (`account`, `item`, `code`, `ok`, `message`). `shared` counts only items the Main Account has.
- Finding: `level` (`ok`|`warn`|`fail`), `account`, `item`, `code` (stable, e.g. `link.real-file`, `link.other-target` (warn), `link.dangling` (fail), `symlink-forbidden` (fail; any link where the item must be a real file or copy), `path.invalid`, `missing`, `copy.stale`, `symlink-forbidden`, `credential.mode`, `json-key.drift`, `json-key.would-remove`, `name.backup-like`, `plugin.error`, `skill.outdated`), `message`, `hint?`, `source` (`core` or plugin name), `fixable`. sideby never re-points a link.
- Quota: `status: "ok"` with `windows[]` (`label` `5h`|`7d`|`<n>m`, `windowMinutes`, `usedPercent`, `resetsAt`), `observedAt`, `source`, `plan?`, `from?` (the account the reading was taken from, when another account of the same login); or `status: "unavailable"` with `reason` `not-enabled`|`no-session`|`unrecognized`|`no-source`|`api-account` and `detail?`.
- Usage: `status: "ok"` with `days`, `sessions`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `totalTokens`, optional `daily[]` (`{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", totalTokens }`, one per local day ending today, oldest first, 0 for days without records; can sum to less than `totalTokens`) and optional `lastActivityAt` (ISO, newest record read); or `unavailable` with `reason` `no-source`|`no-session`|`unrecognized` and `detail?`. Sources: Claude `projects/**/*.jsonl`, Codex `sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl`; Grok and pi have none.
- `new --json`: `{ ok, account, steps[], hookErrors[], nextSteps[], alias?: { name, added, message? }, shellInitFiles?: [{ shell, path, ok, action?: "written"|"unchanged", message? }], suggestion?: { name, alias?, aliasProblem? } }` (`suggestion` only with `--next`).
- `next --json`: `{ family, pick: ref|null, accounts[] (`ref`, `kind`, `state`, `pressure`: number|null, `resetsAt?` for full, `observedAt?`, `quotaFrom?`, `sameLoginAs?`: the current account when this one is its same login, never picked), from?: the current account (`SIDEBY_ACCOUNT`), hasQuota, earliestReset?: { ref, at } }`, best first.
- `alias add|rm --json`: `{ ok, alias, status: "added"|"exists"|"removed"|"absent", account?, args?, shellInitFiles? }`; `ok` is false when a shell-init file was not rewritten.
- `app install --json`: `{ platform, path, files[], mode: "panel"|"url", url?, node, entry, updated, hints[] }`; `app uninstall --json`: `{ platform, removed[], skipped[] (path, reason) }`.
- `quota setup|teardown --json`: setup `{ family, applied, plan: { status: "enabled"|"ready"|"blocked", file, diff, message } }`; teardown `{ family, ok, message, diff? }` (`schemas/quota-setup.json`, `schemas/quota-teardown.json`).
- No output ever contains a credential value.

## Configuration

- File: `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/sideby/config.json` (optional). Fields: `accounts.<ref>.args`, `aliases` (`<short>` → ref, or `{ account, args? }`), `ignore`, `pluginDirs`, `plugins.<name>` (`enabled` plus plugin settings), `extraSharedItems.<family>[]` (`path` relative to the account directory, no `..`; `mode`; optional `noSymlink`, `credential`), `shellInitFile` (`{ zsh?, bash? }`, absolute or `~/` paths sideby keeps equal to `sideby shell-init <shell>`), `resumeRouting` (boolean, default false; Host-named functions that route a resume by id, see `sideby resume`), `accountTitle` (boolean, default false; terminal title `[<SIDEBY_LABEL>]` at launch), `display` (`{ families?: [id], accounts?: { <family>: [name] }, pinned?: { <family>: [name] } }`, the Display Order and Pinned Accounts the Panel's arrange mode and pin menu write; `list` and `quota` follow it, pinned first, then listed, the rest after in their usual order; `list --json` marks pinned accounts `pinned: true`; display only, never the Handoff Order), `quota.check.<family>` (boolean, default true; false stops quota checks that cost a request, such as Grok's), `panel` (`{ theme?: system|light|dark, language?: auto|en|zh }`).
- State: `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/sideby/` (quota cache, last doctor result, original `settings.json` bytes).
- Plugins directory: `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/sideby/plugins/`.
- Share Modes: `link`, `copy`, `link-or-copy`, `link-or-local`, `local`, `local-if-api`, `info`, `json-key`.

## Plugin API

- A plugin is a local directory with `plugin.json` (`name`, `version`, `description`, optional `main`, `userConfig`) and `index.ts` exporting `{ name, register(api) } satisfies Plugin`.
- Loaded from built-ins, then `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/sideby/plugins/*`, then config `pluginDirs`. Directory, `plugin.json` and entry must be owned by the user and not group/other writable.
- A plugin is local code with the user's full permissions.
- Only `import type { Plugin } from 'sideby'`; never import values. Everything arrives through `api`.
- `api.family(def: FamilyDef)`: register a Family (`id`, `title`, `bin`, `installUrl`, `layout`, `selectVar`, `hijackVars`, `apiVars`, `sharedItems`, `login`, optional `logo`, `secretFileMeansApi`, `defaultArgs`, `keepTitle` (`{ args, key }`: Host args that keep the `accountTitle` title, skipped when a user arg contains `key`), `loginState`, `model`, `readQuota`, `readUsage`, `quotaSetup`). A throwing `loginState` or `model` becomes an entry in that account's `problems`.
- `logo: { path, color?, title?, fillRule? }`: the panel's mark for the Family, one SVG path in a 24x24 view box. `path` holds only SVG path data (max 20000 chars), `color` is hex. An invalid logo is dropped with a plugin error; the panel then shows initials.
- `api.on('launch.before', [filter], handler)`: before `run`/`login`; mutate `ctx.env` and `ctx.args`, or `throw api.abort(msg)`. 30 s timeout.
- `api.on('account.create.before', [filter], handler)`: before `new` (CLI or panel) writes anything; `ctx` is `{ family, name, api, accounts, config }` (`accounts`: the family's existing accounts). `throw api.abort(msg)` refuses: the CLI exits 1 with `msg`, the panel answers 400 `{ error, code: 'create-refused' }`. Any other error or the 10 s timeout also stops creation. 10 s.
- `api.on('account.created', [filter], handler)`: after `new`; `ctx.log()` for next steps. 30 s.
- `api.on('doctor.check', [filter], handler)`: return `CheckResult[]` (`level`, `item`, `code`, `message`, `hint?`, `fix?`). 10 s.
- `filter` is `{ family?: string }`. `ctx.config` is the plugin's own settings. `api.fs.writeFileAtomic(path, data, mode?)` for fixes.
- Built-in optional plugin `account-script`: when enabled, runs `<account>/sideby-before-launch` before each launch (25 s limit; failure stops the launch).
- Test plugins with `sideby/testing`: `withFakeHome`, `fakeHost`, `readHostLog`, `snapshot`, `diffSnapshots`.

## Panel settings through the CLI

- `sideby pin|unpin <account|short command> [--json]`: Same Login together, at most 3 per Family; new pins go last; repeated operations are no-ops. JSON: `ref`, `pinned`, `changed`, `message`, `display` (schemas/pin.json, schemas/unpin.json).
- `sideby order [--json]`: `display` and effective `families` with account `name`, `ref`, `pinned` (schemas/order.json). `order <family> <name>...`, `order --families <id>...`, `order --reset` save immediately; reset keeps pins. Unknown or repeated names fail; stale names are removed on write. Display only, not Handoff Order.
- `sideby quota check <family> on|off [--json]`: saves the fetching switch; JSON `family`, `on`, `changed` (schemas/quota-check.json). Local reading continues; CI blocks fetching. `quota [account|family] --refresh` works for every fetching Family.
- `sideby local [on|off] [--yes] [--json]` (ADR-0024, for sideby developers): `running` (`local`, `npm` or null), `local` (the kept Local Build: `version`, `commit`, `dirty`, `builtAt`), `kept` (npm version set aside), `switched` (schemas/local.json). No argument: status, exit 0. `on` links the kept Local Build (no rebuild; `pnpm local` builds), `off` restores the kept npm package or installs `latest`, then runs `sideby update --skill --yes` of the npm code so the skill comes along (`skillSynced`); without `--yes` exit 10, with it switch, restart a background panel (`restartedPanel`), exit 0. `blocked` (exit 1): no Local Build, or not an npm global install.
- `sideby update --skill [--yes] [--json]`: update only the installed sideby skill to this sideby's version; never installs the CLI and asks no registry (says `sideby update` is separate when the last check saw a newer sideby). Without `--yes` exit 10; with it exit 0, or 1 when the skill update failed.
- `sideby update --auto on|off [--json]`: saves Auto Update without checking/installing; JSON `auto`, `changed` (schemas/update-auto.json). Exit 0, no preview; enable only when asked.
- `sideby handoff status --json`: additive `overview` with `settings`, `takeover` decisions and `recent` hand-overs (schemas/handoff-status.json); schemaVersion remains 1.
- Agent instructions: skills/sideby/references/panel.md covers Display Order, pins, model and Remote Control; quota.md, update.md and handoff.md cover the other settings.

AI Tasks (ADR-0027):
- sideby ask [<text>] [--task free|fix|quota|account|host|plugin|terminal|handoff] [--account <ref>] [--terminal <id>] [--attach <file>]... [--print] [--json]: opens the user's terminal, which runs this Node and sideby by absolute path; --print only prints the prompt; --attach (repeatable, at most 5) adds a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image up to 20 MB or an MP4, MOV or WebM video up to 200 MB, type from the file's first bytes (refused: code attachment-type, attachment-too-large, too-many-attachments, attachment-link, attachment-missing), copied to `ai/attachments/<task-id>/` (deleted after 7 days) and listed in the prompt; `--json` gives `attachments: [{ path, kind, bytes }]`; Codex (`FamilyDef.imageArg`) also gets each image as `--image=<path>`; --account (an API account too) becomes `ask.account`, the next default. Exit 1 gives a paste command or prompt, with `reason` (a code: no-accounts, none-signed-in, all-full, not-installed, automation-denied, npx-cache, unsafe-path, failed, unsupported-platform) and `detail` (what to do next). npx-cache: install sideby with `npm i -g sideby` first.
- sideby ask --run <id>: consumes a private task file (expires after one hour), starts the Host in sideby's AI work directory. A prompt task starts as `sideby run` would, but never with the Host's permission checks switched off (ADR-0031, `FamilyDef.aiTaskArgs`): Claude Code drops `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` and `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` and gets `--permission-mode auto` unless another mode is picked; Codex drops `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` and `--yolo`; other families start unchanged. `sideby run` keeps every argument. The text output after opening a terminal adds "Its permission checks stay on, so risky actions are checked first." for such a family.
- sideby ask --spec - [--print] --json (ADR-0030): a Portal starts an AI Task with a Task Spec, one JSON object on stdin (at most 1 MB, never through a shell): `{ specVersion: 1, prompt, cwd?, ... }` (another Tool's Task Prompt; keys stripped again, attachments section appended; `cwd` an existing folder inside HOME by real path, else exit 1 `bad-cwd`; no `cwd` = sideby's task folder, declared as `"cwd": "engine"`) or `{ specVersion: 1, native: { task, text?, context? }, ... }` (sideby's own task, prompt unchanged). Both take lang (en|zh), account, terminal, remember, files (absolute paths, at most 5). Output as `sideby ask --json`; --print gives `{ schemaVersion, prompt, removedSecrets }` (schemas/ask-print.json) and writes nothing. Refused: `{ schemaVersion, error, code, reason }` with spec-invalid, spec-too-large, bad-cwd (exit 1) or spec-version (exit 2: update sideby).
- sideby ask --choices --json: `{ account, accounts: [{ ref, label, signedIn }], terminal, terminals: [{ id, label }], reason, detail }` (schemas/ask-choices.json); account null with reason no-accounts|none-signed-in|all-full.
- createPanelHandler({ ask: { bridge: 'postMessage' } }) (ADR-0030): inside a frame, hides the Panel's "Let AI do it" button and every AI Task entry posts `{ type: 'local-tools:ask', version: 1, preset, native: { task, text, context }, text }` to window.parent at the Panel's own origin. The package root's ai-tasks.json declares sideby's tasks for a Portal (skill, skillInstall, cwd "engine", contribute, one native preset per task with en/zh title, placeholder, examples).
- sideby terminal [--set <id>|--custom '<template>'|--unset] [--json]: terminal discovery and preference. --custom saves terminal.custom (an argv template with both {cmd} and {cwd}) and selects it; --set custom needs one saved. Config terminal.preferred, terminal.custom, ask.account select the defaults.
- sideby key <account> [--var <NAME>] [--json]: hidden TTY input; never send a key to an AI. An empty key writes nothing (exit 1). API accounts and families with secretFileMeansApi: false only.
- sideby try <account> [--yes] [--json]: a short paid Host request, with the same arguments as `sideby run` plus the probe's. Exit 10 asks for confirmation; --yes returns 0/1 with redacted output.
- sideby plugins new <id> [--json]: local Family Plugin skeleton. Plugins run with the user's full permissions.
- sideby plugins check <id|path> [--json]: deterministic validation, exit 0/1, each problem includes a fix.
Schemas: ask.json, terminal.json, key.json, try.json, plugins-new.json, plugins-check.json. All include schemaVersion: 1.

Settings (spec §3.29, ADR-0029):
- sideby autostart [on|off] [--yes] [--json]: start the panel in the background at login (macOS LaunchAgent `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.sideby.panel.plist`, mode 644, `RunAtLoad` true, `KeepAlive` false, ProgramArguments = this Node, this sideby's entry, `ui --background --no-open`, a sideby marker comment). JSON: `supported`, `reason?`, `state` (off, on, stale: a recorded path is gone and `missing` names it, foreign: a file sideby did not write, never touched), `path`, `programArguments?`, `current` (it starts this sideby), and for on/off `action`, `changed`, `applied`, `content?`, `commands` (`launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>`, `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/dev.sideby.panel`), `loaded?`, `note?`. Without --yes a change exits 10; refused exits 1 with code unsupported, foreign, npx-cache, temp-dir or unsafe-path (install with `npm i -g sideby` first). `sideby update` (`refreshedAutostart`) and `pnpm local` rewrite an existing agent; neither creates one.
- sideby config get [<key>] [--json]: without a key, `file` and `keys` (`key` dot path with `<…>` placeholders, `meaning`, `takes`, `value?`, `entries?`); with one, `key`, `set`, `value?`, `meaning`, `takes`.
- sideby config set <key> <value> [--yes] [--json] / config unset <key> [--yes] [--json]: value is JSON when it parses, else text. The whole result must match schemas/config.json (else code bad-value); unknown keys bad-key; `plugins.<name>` settings refused (plugin-config) except `plugins.<name>.enabled`; `accounts.<ref>.args` takes only model and effort arguments. JSON `action`, `key`, `file`, `changed`, `applied`, `before?`, `after?`. Without --yes a change exits 10. Config `panel.theme` (system, light, dark) and `panel.language` (auto, en, zh) are the Panel's appearance.
Schemas: autostart.json, config-get.json, config-set.json.
